summary:
The National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024 authorizes appropriations and establishes policies for the Department of Defense (DoD), Department of Energy, Department of State, and the Intelligence Community for FY2024.

In Division A, the Act authorizes multiyear procurement for up to 13 Virginia-class submarines and 6 Auxiliary Personnel Lighter vessels. It limits the retirement of certain aircraft, prohibiting KC-135 retirements in FY2024, capping F-15E retirements at 68 through 2029, and barring RQ-4 retirements through 2028, while reducing the A-10 minimum inventory from 153 to 135. It prohibits procuring specified munition chemicals from China, Russia, Iran, or North Korea by September 30, 2028. 

Personnel policy changes include making permanent the authority to order retired members to active duty, prohibiting DoD from requiring or prohibiting gender or pronoun identification in official correspondence, and establishing a prohibition—with waiver and penalty provisions—on former members accepting post-service employment with certain foreign governments. It also allows reinstatement for members involuntarily separated solely for COVID-19 vaccine refusal.

The Act requires an Air Force Future Force Design by August 31, 2024, and a feasibility study on transferring National Guard space functions to the Space Force. It modifies the "domestic source" definition under the Defense Production Act to include Australia and the United Kingdom under certain conditions. It requires at least two annual military exercises with Israel and authorizes up to $40,000,000 per fiscal year for clandestine activities and non-conventional assisted recovery. It imposes a one-year prohibition on DoD in-flight refueling for non-U.S. aircraft engaged in Yemen civil war hostilities. 

Cyberspace provisions establish a Strategic Cybersecurity Program and extend AI/ML acquisition authority through FY2029. It requires a strategy for integrated air and missile defense for Hawaii and the Indo-Pacific region. The Act also establishes personnel management rules for the Space Force, designates March 9 as U.S. Hostage and Wrongful Detainee Day, and authorizes the transfer of 7 excess Coast Guard HC-130H aircraft to California for wildfire suppression. It prohibits FY2024 DoD funds for the Wuhan Institute of Virology or EcoHealth Alliance work in China.

Division B authorizes military construction projects, including an $885 million project at Fort Meade, Maryland, and approximately $1.88 billion total for inside-U.S. defense agency construction. It also authorizes Energy Resilience and Conservation Investment Program projects.

Division C authorizes Maritime Administration funding, including $198,500,000 for the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy and $500,000,000 for port infrastructure development, with a restriction prohibiting funds for fully automated cargo handling equipment if it causes a net job loss. It increases the Student Incentive Payment from $8,000 to $16,000 annually.

Division E includes the Preventing Child Sex Abuse Act of 2023. Division F authorizes Department of State programs, including Foreign Service Institute language reporting and internship provisions.

Division G, the Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2024, establishes comprehensive reporting and investigative mechanisms for sexual assault and harassment allegations within the Central Intelligence Agency, including a Special Victim Investigator. It requires the Director of National Intelligence to develop policies for AI acquisition and use, assess civil nuclear energy for intelligence community capabilities, and promote efficient declassification review for records older than 25 years unless certified as harmful to national security.
